_comment: Oracle cases: identical households expressed for both engines. pe_values are frozen from scripts/oracle-pe.py (policyengine_us); scripts/test-oracle.ts asserts our engine matches within tolerance. Population-scale agreement for these programs is separately established in axiom-oracles (co/ca/az/ny SNAP 100% match on Enhanced CPS; FIIT ~99.5%) — these cases pin the app's request-builder layer to the same numbers on concrete households.

cases.description: NY single parent (35) + kids 8 and 5; $2,078/mo earnings; $1,300/mo rent; heating billed separately.
CO single adult (30), zero income, zero shelter costs — maximum allotment case.

CA couple (35/33) + kids 6 and 4; $2,500/mo earnings; $1,800/mo rent; heating billed separately. PE-side TANF is zeroed: PolicyEngine injects CalWORKs (~$466/mo) into SNAP unearned income, a cross-program interaction the single-program run doesn't model.

AZ single 67-year-old; $1,200/mo Social Security; $900/mo rent; utility allowance harmonized to PE's AZ SUA ($323). Fixture-mined AZ defaults (earned income $1,003, shelter $500) are explicitly zeroed/overridden.

Married filing jointly, $95k wages, kids 8 and 5. taxable_income is fed from PE's own figure ($62,800 = $95k minus the 2026 MFJ standard deduction, which the certified FIIT surface takes as an input). filing_status=1 is this encoding's joint code. Subsection-h (current-law CTC) facts set explicitly.
CO Colorado Works (TANF): single caretaker + 2 children, zero income.

NY TANF: family of 3, zero income, NO verified rent. PolicyEngine's ny_tanf models the need standard without a shelter-allowance component; with verified rent our engine adds the shelter allowance ($698 for $1,000 rent) and the engines legitimately diverge, so this case pins the shelter-free scenario both model identically.

MA SNAP: parent (30) + child (4); $1,500/mo earnings; $1,400/mo rent; heating separate. Members carry citizenship; residency comes from the global overlay default. PE TANF zeroed (cross-program injection).
TN SNAP: couple + child (10); $2,200/mo earnings; no claimed shelter costs. Members carry citizenship; residency via global overlay default. PE TANF zeroed.

FIIT EITC: head of household, $18,000 wages, two qualifying children (8 and 5) with abode/TIN facts. earned income flows from employee_compensation_includible_in_gross_income; the SSN gate and full-year flags come from the fact set / overlay. 40% phase-in x $18k = $7,200, below the 2-child maximum.
OASDI employee wage tax on $95,000: 6.2% = $5,890. Annual (calendar-2026) program.

AL SNAP: parent + 2 kids; $1,800/mo earnings; $1,100 rent, no utilities (AL's certified path has no SUA machinery, so utilities are zeroed on both sides). Population-scale AL agreement is 96% — this pins the plain-household class that does agree.
GA SNAP: same household as AL case; GA takes shelter via monthly_allowable_shelter_costs + verification flags.
SC SNAP: same household as AL case.

KS TANF: assistance plan of 3, zero income, shelter group I (the base county group — PolicyEngine models a single statewide standard matching it; our groups III-V encode the county variation PE flattens: $391/$403/$429). Full month (day 1, 31 days) so proration is a no-op.
TX TANF: family of 3, caretaker without second parent, passes recognizable-needs test, eligibility from day 1.
FL SNAP: same plain household as the AL case. Population-scale FL agreement is 91% — this pins the class that does agree.
NC SNAP: same plain household as the AL case.
FIIT single filer, $280k wages, taxable income $263,900 (PE's figure after the single standard deduction). Exercises the upper brackets of the single schedule; agreement to the cent.
FIIT CTC phaseout: MFJ, $420k AGI, 2 qualifying children — $4,400 reduced by $50 per $1,000 over the $400k joint threshold = $3,400.

AK ATAP: assistance unit of 3 (caretaker + 2 kids over two), zero income. Full ak_atap is acknowledged-incomplete on our side and PE's ak_atap adds components beyond the maximum payment, so this pins the table-driven standards both engines encode: need standard, gross income limit (185% test), and maximum payment. Tolerance 1 absorbs PE's unrounded 185% FPL product (3975.65 vs our 3975).
AL TANF: assistance unit of 3, zero income. Our encoding certifies the annual benefit; PE's al_tanf is monthly, so the oracle freezes PE's 2026 annual sum (12 x 344).
GA TANF: assistance unit of 3, zero income, at application. Annual benefit vs PE's 2026 annual sum (12 x 280).
UT FEP: household of 3 (caretaker + 2 minor children), zero income. Pins the payment-standard table; full ut_fep_eligible is acknowledged-incomplete on our side.

IL senior real-estate tax deferral: 70-year-old owner-occupant, income within limits, $4,000 of taxes payable, all statutory application/agreement conditions met. Deferral below the annual cap passes through in full.
IL senior real-estate tax deferral: same senior with $9,000 of taxes payable — both engines cap the deferral at the $7,500 annual maximum.

NY single adult earning $1,400/mo, $400 rent, heating billed separately. Interior value exercising the 20% earned-income deduction, standard deduction, and heating/cooling SUA at household size 1. Note: with NO separate heating costs the engines diverge (ours $24, PE $247.90) because PE applies the heating SUA regardless of the separate-heating flag - scenario documented in excluded.

NY elderly single (70) on $1,800/mo Social Security with $1,800 rent and separate heating: the uncapped excess-shelter deduction for elderly/disabled households drives net income to zero and the benefit to the 1-person maximum allotment on both engines.

AK ATAP: assistance unit of 5 (two adults + kids 8, 5, 2), zero income. Pins the size-5 rows of the need standard and gross income limit. The maximum payment is deliberately NOT compared: our encoding follows the DPA 2026 adult-included family-size chart ($1,127 for size 5) while PE reconstructs it as base + $102 per additional CHILD, undercounting two-adult units ($1,025) - the constructions coincide on single-parent units (see ak-tanf-family3). Report upstream to policyengine-us.
UT FEP: household of 5 (two adults + 3 minor children), zero income. Pins the size-5 payment-standard row.
CO Colorado Works (TANF): single caretaker + 3 children, zero income. Second table row alongside co-tanf-family3.
TX TANF: family of 4, caretaker without second parent, passes recognizable-needs test, eligibility from day 1. Second table row alongside tx-tanf-family3.

IN TANF: child-only assistance group of 1 (participating_members=1), zero income - the one size the sparsely-encoded upstream benefit table (keys 1 and 6) can evaluate, partially lifting the exclusion the same way ks-tanf-family3 pins the KS shelter-group scenario. federal_income_poverty_level is fed as an input for the gross test (moot at zero income). Both the new-application and ongoing benefits equal PE's in_tanf.
Childless EITC: single 25-year-old earning $10,000 - exercises the childless credit table and the age/abode eligibility gates, distinct from the with-children table pinned by fiit-eitc-hoh-2kids.

EITC phase-out region: HoH with 2 qualifying children at $40,000 AGI - the credit is deep into the 21.06% phase-out and both engines agree to the cent ($3,923.23), complementing the plateau case at $18,000.

AZ elderly single with $300/mo verified medical expenses on top of the az-snap-elderly scenario: both engines deduct actual-minus-$35 ($265) and reach the 1-person maximum. $300 sits above AZ's $180 SMD gross threshold where the standard and actual branches coincide; in the $35-$180 range the engines diverge because our chain does not compose the state SMD output (see excluded).

excluded.reason: Pilot pipeline takes NY bracket floors/rates and the standard deduction as inputs; feeding them would test arithmetic, not encoded law.
Payment-standard chain takes federal poverty levels as inputs (parameter-as-input); no meaningful oracle without supplying the law values.
Requires KS county shelter-group selection (shelter_group_i..v) not yet mapped to PolicyEngine's model.
CalWORKs encoding takes maximum_aid_payment_under_section_11450 and the COLA as inputs (parameter-as-input); no meaningful oracle without supplying the law values.

Upstream table cash_assistance_maximum_monthly_benefit_for_recipient_parent_or_caretaker_ag_table is sparsely encoded (keys 1 and 6 only) — participating_members=3 cannot evaluate. Upstream filing. Size-1 (child-only) row now pinned by in-tanf-child-only; sizes 2-5 remain blocked.

policyengine-us ME maximum-benefit table is stale: missing the 2025-10-01 COLA (PE $895 for size 3 at 2026-07 vs $917 in the encoded FY-2026 table). Our value is the current one; report upstream to policyengine-us.
policyengine-us has no md_tanf variable (engine-side value $773 is pinned in test:regression instead).
Encoding takes payment_standard_for_family and federal_poverty_level as inputs (parameter-as-input); no meaningful oracle without supplying the law values. No upstream filing yet.
Encoding takes appropriate_eligibility_standard and applicable_budget_standard as inputs (parameter-as-input); no meaningful oracle without supplying the law values. No upstream filing yet.

Earner scenarios only: our encoding applies a 20% work-expense rate sourced to the 2007 DHR payment manual, while policyengine-us applies 30% per Ala. Admin. Code r. 660-2-2-.30(2) (eff. 2022-05-15) - $184 vs $204/mo benefit on $200/mo earnings. Our rate appears stale; report upstream to the AL rulespec repo. Zero-income cases (al-tanf-family3) are unaffected and pinned.

Above-base scenarios only: oasdi_wage_tax is rate x statutory 'wages' taken as input; the 26 USC 3121(a)(1) excess-remuneration exclusion is encoded on the Payment entity but not composed into the tax, so a $250k wage yields $15,500 vs PE's capped $11,439. Below-base cases (oasdi-wage-95k) are unaffected and pinned. Report composition gap upstream to rulespec-us.

No-utility scenarios only: policyengine-us applies the NY heating/cooling SUA even when the household reports no heating costs separate from rent (PE $247.90 vs our $24 for a single earner at $1,400/mo with $400 rent and no separate utilities). Separate-heating scenarios agree and are pinned (ny-snap-family3, ny-snap-earner-1400). Needs upstream clarification of PE's SUA gating.

Two-adult maximum-payment scenarios only: policyengine-us rebuilds the DPA family-size chart as base + $102 per additional child, undercounting two-adult units ($1,025 vs the chart's $1,127 for size 5). Single-parent max payment (ak-tanf-family3) and the size-keyed need standard / gross income limit (ak-tanf-family5) are pinned.

Standard-medical-deduction range only ($35-$180/mo of expenses): the AZ module correctly computes the $145 SMD as a certified output (medical_deduction), but the net-income chain composes the federal 7 CFR 273.10 excess-medical module fed by raw snap_total_medical_expenses (actual minus $35) instead - $150/mo of expenses yields a $115 deduction vs PE's $145. Above $180 the branches coincide and are pinned (az-snap-elderly-medical). Same encoded-but-not-composed genre as the OASDI finding.
